original_question: Let G be a cubic planar graph and let L be a 3-list-assignment on G, meaning each vertex has a list of three allowed colors. An L-coloring is proper if adjacent vertices receive different colors, and two L-colorings are disjoint if every vertex receives different colors in the two colorings. Must every such 3-list-assignment admit two disjoint proper L-colorings?
target_in_paper: Section 2 ("Various open problems related to list packing"), subsection "Planar bipartite graphs", Problem 2.3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2411.10046v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core combinatorial content: a 3-list-assignment on a cubic planar graph, the notions of proper and disjoint L-colourings, and the question of whether two disjoint proper colourings from the same lists must exist.
missing_details: The paper places the question inside the subsection "Planar bipartite graphs" and introduces it immediately after citing the Alon-Tarsi result for planar bipartite graphs, so the intended stand-alone formulation should make the bipartite hypothesis explicit rather than leave it implicit. This is an inference from the nearby context, but it is the paper-faithful way to make the question non-elliptic. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2411.10046v1))
The universal quantifiers should be stated explicitly: for every graph G in the intended class and for every 3-list-assignment L on V(G). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2411.10046v1))

To be fully self-contained, it helps to write the two colourings as maps from V(G) choosing colours from the same list assignment L, and to state separately that each colouring is proper and that they are vertexwise distinct. The paper defines these notions just before Problem 2.3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2411.10046v1))
refined_question: Let G be a cubic planar bipartite graph, and let L assign to each vertex v a list L(v) of exactly three available colours. Must there exist two colourings φ, ψ of V(G) such that φ(v), ψ(v) ∈ L(v) for every v ∈ V(G), each of φ and ψ is proper (that is, φ(u) ≠ φ(v) and ψ(u) ≠ ψ(v) for every edge uv ∈ E(G)), and φ(v) ≠ ψ(v) for every vertex v?
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 2.3. In Section 2 the paper first defines list-assignments, proper L-colourings, and disjoint L-colourings, and then, under the subsection heading "Planar bipartite graphs", asks whether for a 3-list-assignment of a cubic planar graph one can choose two disjoint proper colourings. Because the problem is embedded in that bipartite subsection and motivated immediately by the planar-bipartite 3-choosability result of Alon and Tarsi, I have made bipartiteness explicit in the refined stand-alone version; that is the closest sharp formulation to the paper's actual intent. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2411.10046v1))
